History and Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
56-year-old man with hypertension, active tobacco and alcohol use, and strong family cardiac history presents with acute, ongoing central chest pressure radiating to left arm/shoulder with diaphoresis, nausea, dyspnea; clinically concerning for acute coronary syndrome—ambulance activated for immediate ED evaluation.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Central chest pressure “like someone sitting on my chest” started a couple of hours ago while gardening (light activity); pain remains present.  
• Radiation: Left arm and shoulder.  
• Associated symptoms: Nausea (no vomiting), diaphoresis, shortness of breath, subjective tachycardia/palpitations (attributed to stress).  
• First episode; no prior similar events.  
• No noted triggers beyond light gardening; no relief reported.  
• Review of systems otherwise not discussed.

Past Medical History:
• Hypertension (onset date, control, and complications not documented).  
• Overweight/obesity (BMI not documented).

Medications:
• None documented.

Allergies:
• Aspirin – mild allergic swelling; not life-threatening.

Social History:
• Tobacco: 10 cigarettes/day for 15 years (current smoker).  
• Alcohol: ~7–8 pints of beer/week.  
• Recreational drugs: not mentioned.  
• Exercise: Minimal activity.  
• Living situation: Lives alone; house currently unattended.  
• Occupation: Restaurant owner (sushi shop).

Family History:
• Father: Fatal myocardial infarction at ~age 60.  
• Mother: “Heart problems” (details not provided).

Physical Examination:
(Virtual encounter; limited)  
• General: Patient appears sweaty; still experiencing chest discomfort.  
• No additional examination findings or vital signs documented.

Investigations:
• None performed yet; ambulance team instructed to obtain pre-hospital ECG.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome (rule-out myocardial infarction)  
  • Assessment: Classic ischemic chest pain with radiation, autonomic symptoms, multiple risk factors, positive family history.  
  • Plan:  
    – EMS activated; patient kept on line until arrival.  
    – Pre-hospital ECG and cardiac monitoring.  
    – Hospital transfer for definitive evaluation and management (labs, serial ECGs, troponins, imaging).  
    – Communicate aspirin allergy to EMS/ED; consider risk–benefit if ASA indicated.  
    – Advise patient to keep front door open for EMS access.

Issue 2 – Cardiovascular Risk Factors (hypertension, smoking, alcohol, obesity)  
  • Assessment: Long-standing hypertension, active smoking, excess weight, moderate alcohol intake.  
  • Plan: To be addressed after acute event; anticipate need for risk-factor modification, smoking cessation counseling, weight management, alcohol use discussion, and possible lipid screening.

General Plan Items  
  • Follow-up with primary care/cardiology after hospital discharge.  
  • Ensure documentation of medication list and allergy in hospital record.

Quality checks:

Missing but expected elements:
• Complete medication reconciliation.  
• Baseline vitals (BP, HR, RR, O2 sat, temperature).  
• Detailed review of systems, physical exam, and past surgical history.

Internal conflicts: None noted.

Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal extraneous content.
